chunks: From him, from Salih, from Al-Washa’, from Karraam, from Abdullah Bin Talha who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the lizard, so he (peace be upon him) said: ‘Filthy, and it is a metamorphosed (creature), all of them. So if you were to kill it, wash yourself (Ghusl)’.

My father was seated in Al-Hijr, and with him was a man to whom he was narrating. So a lizard started ululating with its tongue. So my father said to the man: ‘Do you know what this lizard is saying?’ He said, ‘I have no knowledge of what it is saying’. He (peace be upon him) said: ‘It is saying that if you mention Usman by insults, I will insult Ali (peace be upon him) until he goes from there’.
He (peace be upon him) said: ‘And my father said: ‘There is none from the Clan of Umayya who dies, but he gets metamorphosed as a lizard.’

He (peace be upon him) said: ‘Abdul Malik Bin Marwaan, when death descended upon him, was metamorphosed into a lizard in front of the children who were in his presence. So when he was lost, that was a great (problem) for them as they did not know what to do.

Then they met in a gathering, and decided to take a trunk and make it to look like a man. So they did that and clothed that with a coat of iron armour. Then they wrapped it in the shroud. So no one from the people knew about it except for myself and his children’.

key_terms.الْحِجْرُ: Al-Hijr (a specific area in the Prophet's mosque)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing a lizard and what is the significance of maskh in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) classifies the lizard (wazagh) as 'rij's' (filthy) and 'maskh' (metamorphosed), linking its physical nature to spiritual corruption, particularly among the Umayyads. The narrative illustrates the concept of 'maskh' by recounting how Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan transformed into a lizard upon death, a phenomenon interpreted as divine retribution for their deviation and enmity toward Ahl al-Bayt. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Umayyads as archetypal examples of those who lost their human form due to their moral and political transgressions.
